Prosecutors found that Vaught overrode a computer system when she couldn’t find Versed and instead chose the first medication on the list beginning with V-E, then ignored the red cap on the vecuronium bromide that states “Warning: Paralyzing Agent.” She told investigators later that she had been “distracted with something.” She was sentenced on May 13 to three years’ probation.

docs.lead_paragraph: It is one thing to know that Louise Bourgeois made paintings. There are often a few of them in surveys of her long career as a sculptor, which reached its apogee in the 1980s and ’90s. It is something else to learn that in the 1940s — her first decade in New York — she made more than 100 paintings. Nearly half of them are now heating up a large gallery at the Metropolitan Museum of Art with raw emotion, awkward paint handling and adamantine colors — most often brilliant to dark shades of blue and especially red.
